arguments.sql_query:
-- Step 1: Identify standard SSRI drugs in our cohort
SELECT 
    c.concept_id,
    c.concept_name,
    c.standard_concept,
    COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS patient_count
FROM omop.concept c
JOIN omop.drug_strength ds ON c.concept_id = ds.drug_concept_id
JOIN omop.drug_exposure de ON ds.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
WHERE c.vocabulary_id = 'RxNorm' 
  AND LOWER(c.concept_name) IN (
    'citalopram', 'escitalopram', 'fluoxetine', 'fluvoxamine', 
    'paroxetine', 'sertraline', 'duloxetine'
  )
GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.standard_concept
ORDER BY patient_count DESC;

content.text: Good point — my direct concept IDs for SSRIs didn't match the exposure data directly. Let me investigate the actual SSRI representations in our cohort and understand the mappings between RxNorm and SNOMED/ICD codes for indications and side effects.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT TOP 30 de.drug_concept_id, c.concept_name, c.vocabulary_id, COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS person_count, COUNT(*) AS exposure_count
FROM omop.drug_exposure de
JOIN omop.concept c ON de.drug_concept_id = c.concept_id AND STANDARD_CONCEPT IS NOT NULL
WHERE c.standard_concept IN ('S', 'C') AND c.domain_id IN ('Drug', 'Clinical Drug')
	AND (
		LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%citalopram%' 
		OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%fluoxetine%' 
		OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%paroxetine%'  
		OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%sertraline%'
		OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%escitalopram%'
		OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%fluvoxamine%'
	)
GROUP BY de.drug_concept_id, c.concept_name, c.vocabulary_id
ORDER BY person_count DESC;
